entities.summary: Bernardus Papiensis, also known as Bernard of Pavia or Bernard Balbi, was an Italian canonist and bishop of the Catholic Church. Born into a prominent family in Pavia, Italy, Bernardus studied at the University of Bologna, where he earned a degree in law and was ordained as a priest. He later became a prominent figure in the Catholic Church, serving as the Bishop of Pavia from 1206 to 1213. Bernardus was a key figure in the development of canon law, producing several influential treatises on the subject, including the 'Decretum Gratiani'. His work had a lasting impact on the Church's governance and jurisprudence, shaping the course of medieval ecclesiastical law. Bernardus' legacy extends beyond his contributions to canon law, as he played a significant role in the political landscape of medieval Italy, serving as an advisor to several nobles and monarchs. His influence can also be seen in the development of the Papal States, which would eventually become a major power in Italy. As a bishop, Bernardus was also involved in various ecclesiastical reforms, including the establishment of a new diocesan system in Pavia. Through his writings and actions, Bernardus left a lasting mark on the Catholic Church and the world of medieval law.
